output.summary: A flowering herbaceous perennial native to Europe, Western Asia and North Africa, marsh mallow is covered in soft hairs and bears pale pink or lilac flowers. Its young leaves can be cooked, flower buds pickled, and roots boiled before frying or boiled and sweetened for candy.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves are cooked, buds pickled, and roots boiled before frying or sweetened for candy; marsh mallow was historically a Roman delicacy.
